finding: a defect in my own closing procedure: step 3 would archive a truncated JUnit set
howItSurfaced: Checking that each closing step's precondition was ready. Step 4 archives build/test-results/test, and the question was whether step 3's runGameTest regenerates that directory.

theAnswer.method: gradlew test --dry-run, and reading its dependency graph
theAnswer.result: The graph is compileTestJava, processTestResources, testClasses, testClasspathBridge, test - runGameTest is not in it
theAnswer.meaning: test and runGameTest are independent tasks. runGameTest writes build/reports/gametest/results.xml only; the JUnit XML in build/test-results/test comes from test alone.

theDefect: Step 3 ran runGameTest, and step 4 then archived build/test-results/test. Since runGameTest does not run test, step 4 would have archived whatever was already there - which today is a single XML left by two filtered spot-check runs, not 103 files covering 629 tests. The procedure would have filed a truncated set as the full record, which is the same failure it was written to prevent.
theFix: Step 3 now runs gradlew test runGameTest, with a note saying why both are needed and that the independence was verified by dry run.
whyThisIsWorthRecording: The step was added two rounds ago specifically to stop a spot check from destroying the full results. It would have preserved the wreckage instead, and only a precondition check caught it - the step read correctly when I wrote it.
